65 tests make 105 process calls; top ten are 36%

label: The work is spread rather than concentrated: 65 tests make 105 process-shaped calls and the ten heaviest account for only 36%, while nine tests make none at all.
sources: measured: static per-test count over .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/tests/upgrade-legacy.vitest.ts -> 65 tests, 105 calls, top-10 share 36%, 9 tests with zero

label: The heaviest tests are dirty-tree-writes-manifest and stale-manifest-head-refuses-apply at six calls each, so no single test dominates the file.

Each of the 105 calls is a chain rather than one process: node upgrade-legacy.mjs, then bash validate.sh per packet, then two node processes per validation, so one call costs roughly four to ten processes.
The reset is the second component and is paid 58 times: git reset --hard over a 3115-file repository, six path removals, and a utimes pass over 734 dist files.
sources: measured: 734 files under a dist path

label: Because both components scale with the number of tests rather than with a few heavy ones, sharding divides both: N shards each with its own sandbox take about 1/N of the calls and resets, and the only new cost is N sandbox copies instead of one.
The estimated result is about 400 s down to roughly 100-140 s at four shards, dominated by the per-shard beforeAll copy plus a quarter of the test work, and it must be measured before it is claimed.

direction: Cutting individual heavy tests in upgrade-legacy
reason: The top ten tests are only 36% of the process calls, so removing them would not halve the file
